controls.capability: Security-by-design expectations are formalized in release gates and governance evidence
Owner responsibility and privileged authority are explicitly assigned and enforced
Security and release status are communicated through health, readiness, and governance evidence
Internal control information is versioned with source, test, owner, status, and release context
Security, privacy, supply-chain, resilience, and operational risks are evaluated before release
Material changes trigger branch validation, preview builds, deployed-system tests, and rollback checks
Control operation is monitored through runtime scans, health evidence, deployed gates, and error review
Control deficiencies block release and require repair before production promotion
Automated control activities cover identity, billing, entitlements, usage, containment, privacy, and release integrity
Technology controls are embedded into application routes and mandatory CI workflows
Logical access is restricted through Clerk authentication, organization binding, entitlements, and owner allowlists
Authentication uses passwordless methods, passkeys, enterprise SSO, and recent reverification
Access changes and removals are enforced through subscription suspension, service disablement, and session or token revocation
System boundaries are protected through product-bound service credentials, rate limits, and signed entitlement tokens
Data transmission and session authenticity use TLS-hosted services and signed short-lived session-bound tokens
Vulnerabilities and threats are identified through supply-chain, security-resilience, browser, and runtime checks
Anomalies are monitored through runtime errors, validation abuse controls, and health telemetry
Security events are evaluated and contained through token, session, organization, and service-level controls
Incident response actions are owner-authorized, step-up protected, idempotent, durable, and auditable
Changes require source control, automated gates, preview deployment, build validation, and rollback evidence
Business, technology, supplier, and operational risks are mitigated through isolation, fail-closed dependencies, and release controls
Availability commitments are supported through multi-target parity, health monitoring, timeout bounds, and rollback readiness
Confidential data and secrets are protected through no-store responses, redacted telemetry, scoped credentials, and server-only modules
Billing, entitlement, usage, and release processing use validation, idempotency, bounded inputs, and audit evidence
Privacy governance, data minimization, retention, access, and evidence controls are represented in the privacy crosswalk
